The existing same-message MODIFY already captures cross-location design consistency; brand colors and positioning remain owned by the source Requirement.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey! Here is the vision I have for the website.

The objective is to create a national brand website for SMASH ROOM that can accommodate multiple locations and support future franchise growth.

Primary Website:
[URL_006]

I would like a clean, modern, mobile-friendly design with simplicity comparable to iSmashUSA. The branding should use black, purple, and white, with large images, generous spacing, and straightforward navigation.

Sections for the Homepage:

Hero Banner
Location Selector
Rage Rooms
Axe Throwing
Splatter Room
Corporate Events
Birthday Parties
Reviews
FAQ
Contact

The homepage needs to show visitors our offerings right away and let them choose their location.

Locations at Present:

Fairfield, CA
San Francisco, CA
Seattle, WA

Every location should have a dedicated page of its own, while the design and branding remain consistent across all locations.

The site should be structured so that future locations can be added easily without requiring a redesign.

Possible future examples:

Phoenix
Denver
Austin
Franchise Locations

Overall, it should feel like a national entertainment brand rather than a local business website.

value_updates.template_reuse_strategy: Reuse one website format across location sites while keeping design and SMASH ROOM branding consistent across all locations.

decisions.reason: Brand colors, cross-location branding, and national positioning do not change the independently specified homepage section composition.
The brand identity change does not alter location-selector behavior, available locations, or routing destinations.
Consistent customer-facing branding does not change the separate Wix-site and Wix-account architecture.
The branding decision does not change the Wix booking platform or the use of sibling location sites as booking hosts.
Consistent branding across locations does not alter the required isolation of bookings, revenue, sales, calendars, accounts, or reporting.
The brand identity change does not modify the policy of retaining packages and prices across reused location-site formats.
Customer-facing brand consistency does not change the separate payment setups and payouts required for each location.
